subject: Oceanography
title: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch
description: Learn The Great Pacific Garbage Patch in one minute.

hook.text: The Great Pacific Garbage Patch is not a solid island—it's a soup of tiny plastic pieces spanning 1.6 million km².

buildup.text: Ocean gyres trap floating debris in their calm centers—concentrating plastic from across the Pacific.

discovery.text: 80% of the plastic comes from land—carried by rivers, wind, and coastal runoff into the open ocean.

twist.text: Most of the patch is invisible from the surface—tiny fragments suspended in the water column, not a visible heap.

climax.text: There are now five major garbage patches in the world's oceans—one in each subtropical gyre.

punchline.text: You can't see the garbage patch—but it's three times the size of France.

quiz.question: What does the Great Pacific Garbage Patch look like?
options: A soup of tiny plastic fragments, mostly invisible from the surface
